beats.text: Your {appointments}appointments and your {mail}mail, right on your desktop. K-Desktop {reminds}reminds you, and can act on them.
Let's see {agenda}the Agenda, {connect}connecting your calendars, and {inbox}your mail.
The {agenda}Agenda shows the appointments of {all}all your calendars, day by day, with {today}today always on top. The one {now}happening now is marked, and online meetings get a {join}Join button.
Or switch to the {month}month view. Each {colours}calendar has its own colour, and a click {hide}hides it or shows it again.

{new}New event: a {title}title, the {calendar}calendar, when it {starts}starts and ends, and whether it {repeats}repeats: daily, every weekday, monthly. Then a {reminder}reminder, a {place}place, or a {link}meeting link.
When it's time, K-Desktop {reminds}reminds you, the way you choose: an {osd}on-screen message, a {notification}notification with Join, or one of your {assistant}assistants says it.
In {settings}Settings, Calendar, you keep your {own}own calendars. {newcal}New calendar adds another, each with its {reminder}reminder for new events.
To see one you already have, {subscribe}subscribe to its .ics address: Google, Outlook, {holidays}holidays or sports. It's read-only, and the address is kept {encrypted}encrypted.
To see and edit your Google Calendar, {connect}connect your Google account. Google asks for your own {app}app, a free Client ID, and a {guide}step-by-step guide gets you one, {once}just once.
In {settings}Settings, Mail, K-Desktop {matters}tells you what matters, fires {events}events, and lets the assistant {searches}search, sum up and draft. It's {client}not a mail client.

{add}Add account: type your {address}address, and the {servers}servers fill in by themselves. Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an {password}app password, and the {guide}guide says where to make it. Then {test}Test.
Each account can notify you about {every}every new mail, or {only}only important ones: from the {senders}senders, or with the {words}words in the subject that you list here.
And just like reminders, you pick {how}how you hear about it.

One last tip: both are {events}events too. {before}Ten minutes before an online meeting, {dnd}pause the music and {teams}open Teams. Or when the {bill}electricity bill arrives, {save}save its PDF in a folder, and let you know.
